name: What are the biggest hidden costs in a primary bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: What hidden problems usually increase the price of a primary bathroom remodel after demolition starts?
mainEntity.text: What hidden problems usually increase the price of a primary bathroom remodel after demolition starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest hidden costs usually appear after demolition. Common surprises include water damage around the shower, rotted subfloors, outdated plumbing lines, undersized electrical circuits, mold behind finishes, and framing that is out of level or out of plumb. In older Los Angeles homes, these issues are especially common because past remodels may have used outdated materials or incomplete waterproofing methods. A contractor should inspect as much as possible before demo, but no one can see every condition behind finished walls. That is why a contingency budget matters. Homeowners should also ask how hidden conditions are priced before construction begins so there are no disputes later. A detailed scope, photos, and allowances for uncertain items help keep the project under control.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden costs in a primary bathroom remodel often come from water damage, subfloor repair, outdated plumbing, electrical upgrades, mold remediation, and uneven framing. Older Los Angeles homes can also reveal insufficient waterproofing or venting problems. A contingency budget is important because these issues are often not visible until walls and floors are opened.
